name: Cohesive Marker Profiling
description: Analyzes the frequency, variety, and structural placement of discourse markers (e.g., 'Furthermore', 'Moreover', 'Consequently'). AI heavily relies on a narrow, formulaic set of formal transition words to mechanically stitch paragraphs together.
mechanism: Large Language Models are optimized to produce text that is structurally sound, logical, and easy to follow. A major side effect of this optimization is the over-reliance on explicit cohesive devices—specifically, formal discourse markers. When transitioning between ideas or paragraphs, AI models disproportionately favor a rigid, almost academic vocabulary: 'Additionally', 'Furthermore', 'Moreover', 'However', and famously, 'In conclusion'. They also tend to place these markers exclusively at the very beginning of sentences (sentence-initial position). Human writers, by contrast, use a much wider variety of transitional strategies, frequently embedding markers in the middle of sentences (sentence-medial) or relying on implicit logical flow without needing a signpost word for every new thought. This method scans the text against a comprehensive lexicon of 150+ discourse markers, tracking both their frequency per sentence and their positional distribution. It then uses Jensen-Shannon divergence to compare this profile against known baselines for human writing. A text that is rigidly held together by a repetitive scaffold of 'Firstly', 'Secondly', 'Furthermore', and 'Finally' exhibits a strong AI signature.
useCase: Detecting AI generation in essays, articles, and reports where the transitions between paragraphs feel unnaturally rigid, forced, or overly formal (often referred to as 'AI transition words').
strengths:
• Highly effective at identifying the 'five-paragraph essay' structural formula that LLMs frequently default to.
• Captures high-level text organization patterns that go beyond simple vocabulary checks.
• Very visible and interpretable to users, as words like 'Furthermore' have become widely recognized memes of AI writing.
limitations:
• Heavily dependent on the specific language and genre being analyzed (e.g., actual academic papers naturally use more formal transitions than blogs).
• Simple to evade if the prompt engineer specifically instructs the AI to 'avoid words like furthermore and moreover'.
• Requires a meticulously curated taxonomy of discourse markers tailored to each language.
parameters:
Analysis: Positional Extraction (Initial/Medial/Final) & Marker Lexicon Mapping
Metric: Normalized Frequency & Jensen-Shannon Divergence from Human Baselines
Output: 0-100 Transition Rigidity (Formulaic Cohesion) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-85%. An excellent surface-level forensic tool that exposes the algorithmic scaffolding used by LLMs to simulate logical flow.

references.title: Kumarage, T. et al. (2023). Stylometric Detection of AI-Generated Text in Twitter Timelines. arXiv.
Halliday, M. A. K. & Hasan, R. (1976). Cohesion in English. Longman.
